\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{কবুল} \bn{করা} (kôbul kôrā)}{কবুল করা (kôbul kôrā)}]{\bn{কবুল} \bn{করা} (kôbul kôrā) — to confess; to own up}

\label{lesson:BN-C284-kobul-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for an investigation, then the Bengali for a police inspector.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{কবুল} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{কবুল} \bn{করা}} — \emph{kôbul kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to confess; to own up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{অনেক} \bn{প্রশ্নের} \bn{পরে} \bn{চোর} \bn{অপরাধ} \bn{কবুল} \bn{করল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ônek prôshner pôre chor ôpôrādh kôbul kôrlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After many questions the thief confessed to the crime.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{চোর} \bn{অপরাধ} \bn{কবুল} \bn{করল}, \emph{sei chor ôpôrādh kôbul kôrlô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{কবুল} \bn{করা}} (\emph{kôbul kôrā}) puts \bn{কবুল} — usually traced through Persian to Arabic \emph{qabūl}, 'acceptance' — before \bn{করা}: to accept the charge as true, to confess.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kôbul kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kôbul kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ônek prôshner pôre chor ôpôrādh kôbul kôrlô.} — After many questions the thief confessed to the crime.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for an investigation, then the Bengali for a police inspector, then say \emph{kôbul kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{কবুল} \bn{করা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To confess; to own up\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সূত্র} (sūtrô)}{সূত্র (sūtrô)}]{\bn{সূত্র} (sūtrô) — a clue; a lead}

\label{lesson:BN-C284-sutro}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a police inspector, then the Bengali for to confess.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সূত্র}}
\textbf{\bn{সূত্র}} — \emph{sūtrô} — \textquotedblleft{}a clue; a lead\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{পুলিশ} \bn{জানালার} \bn{কাছে} \bn{একটা} \bn{সূত্র} \bn{পেল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pulish jānālār kāchhe ekṭā sūtrô pelô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police found a clue near the window.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সূত্র}} (\emph{sūtrô}) is Sanskrit \emph{sūtra}, 'a thread, a line' (Monier-Williams); in a mystery it is the thread you follow. \textbf{\bn{সুতো}}, thread, is the everyday word from the same source.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sūtrô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sūtrô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pulish jānālār kāchhe ekṭā sūtrô pelô.} — The police found a clue near the window.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a police inspector, then the Bengali for to confess, then say \emph{sūtrô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{সূত্র} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A clue; a lead\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{পাহারা} \bn{দেওয়া} (pāhārā deoyā)}{পাহারা দেওয়া (pāhārā deoyā)}]{\bn{পাহারা} \bn{দেওয়া} (pāhārā deoyā) — to guard; to keep watch}

\label{lesson:BN-C284-pahara-deoya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to confess, then the Bengali for a clue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{পাহারা} \bn{দেওয়া}}
\textbf{\bn{পাহারা} \bn{দেওয়া}} — \emph{pāhārā deoyā} — \textquotedblleft{}to guard; to keep watch\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{সারারাত} \bn{পুলিশ} \bn{বাড়িটা} \bn{পাহারা} \bn{দিল।}
\end{quote}

\emph{sārārāt pulish bāṛiṭā pāhārā dilô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{কুকুর} \bn{বাড়ি} \bn{পাহারা} \bn{দিল}, \emph{sei kukur bāṛi pāhārā dilô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{পাহারা} \bn{দেওয়া}} (\emph{pāhārā deoyā}) puts \bn{পাহারা} — usually traced to Persian \emph{pahra}, a watch or a guard — before \bn{দেওয়া}: to give watch, to stand guard.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{কয়েদি} (kôyedi)}{কয়েদি (kôyedi)}]{\bn{কয়েদি} (kôyedi) — a prisoner}

\label{lesson:BN-C284-koyedi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a clue, then the Bengali for to guard.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{কয়েদি}}
\textbf{\bn{কয়েদি}} — \emph{kôyedi} — \textquotedblleft{}a prisoner\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{গতকাল} \bn{রাতে} \bn{জেল} \bn{থেকে} \bn{কয়েদিরা} \bn{পালাল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{gôtôkāl rāte jel theke kôyedirā pālālô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Last night prisoners escaped from the jail.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{কয়েদি}} (\emph{kôyedi}) is usually traced through Persian to Arabic \emph{qaidī}, one held in fetters, from \emph{qaid}, a fetter.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kôyedi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gôtôkāl rāte jel theke kôyedirā pālālô.} — Last night prisoners escaped from the jail.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a clue, then the Bengali for to guard, then say \emph{kôyedi} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{জামিন} (jāmin)}{জামিন (jāmin)}]{\bn{জামিন} (jāmin) — bail}

\label{lesson:BN-C284-jamin}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to guard, then the Bengali for a prisoner.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{জামিন}}
\textbf{\bn{জামিন}} — \emph{jāmin} — \textquotedblleft{}bail\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দুই} \bn{দিন} \bn{পরে} \bn{আদালত} \bn{তাকে} \bn{জামিন} \bn{দিল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dui din pôre ādālôt tāke jāmin dilô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Two days later the court granted him bail.
\end{quote}

\bn{জামিন} \bn{দেওয়া}, to grant bail; \bn{জামিন} \bn{পাওয়া}, to get bail.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{জামিন}} (\emph{jāmin}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{zāmin}, 'a surety', a word Persian took from Arabic; it is the guarantee that lets a prisoner go home until the trial.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jāmin}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jāmin}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dui din pôre ādālôt tāke jāmin dilô.} — Two days later the court granted him bail.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to guard, then the Bengali for a prisoner, then say \emph{jāmin} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{জামিন} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Bail\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
